title: Cache penetration, breakdown and avalanche
context: What are cache penetration, cache breakdown and cache avalanche, and how do you handle them?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Penetration is repeated requests for keys that don't exist, which always reach the database. Cache empty results for a short time, and use a Bloom filter to reject impossible keys. Breakdown is a single hot key expiring, so many requests hit the database at once. Use a mutex or single-flight lock so one request reloads it, or never expire hot keys. Avalanche is many keys expiring together. Add random jitter to TTLs and keep the cache layer highly available.

points.title: Penetration
points.why: Missing keys are never cached, so each request goes to the database.

points.title: Breakdown
points.why: A hot key expiring triggers a stampede. One reload with a lock prevents it.

points.title: Avalanche
points.why: Keys with the same TTL expire together. Random jitter spreads the load.
